description:
**Every private repository in this portfolio has had dead CI for an unknown period, and nothing anywhere said so.** Measured 2026-08-25.

```
praxis      PUBLIC    success  2026-08-15
pinakes     PUBLIC    success  2026-08-25
talos       PRIVATE   failure  2026-08-24
cuneiform   PRIVATE   failure  2026-08-25
vita        PRIVATE   failure  2026-08-25
```

All three private failures are byte-identical and none is a code problem: *"The job was not started because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased."* GitHub Actions minutes are free for public repositories and billed for private ones, so the account-level block silently killed CI on every private repo while the public ones kept working.

**vita carried a second, independent version of the same fault.** Its workflow triggers only `on: pull_request` and `workflow_dispatch`. chief merges branches into main LOCALLY and pushes main — it never opens a pull request — so no event that chief generates could ever start that workflow. vita's CI had therefore never run once in the repository's history, and a tasklist (`72`) was unparked and merged as `auto-verified` on the premise that it had.

**This is the generalized form of two failures already recorded in this portfolio.** `amphora` merged three tasklists against a `.chief/verify.sh` that ran one unrelated check and then `exit 0`. `145-forge-harness-gate` was written because *"a green gate that cannot go red is worse than no gate."* Both concern a gate that CANNOT FAIL. This one is worse: a gate that **never executes** is indistinguishable, from every surface chief offers, from one that ran and passed.

**Scope discipline.** chief must not become a CI client, must not require a network call on the merge path, and must not fail a merge because a third-party service is down. What it can do is refuse to let ABSENCE read as SUCCESS — the same distinction `.chief/verify.sh` already draws locally between a skipped check and a passing one, applied to the gate a repo claims to have but does not run.

userStories.title: A declared gate that never ran is reported, not assumed
acceptanceCriteria: chief can tell an operator, per repo, that the repository DECLARES a CI gate (a `.github/workflows/*.yml` or equivalent) whose most recent run is absent, failed to start, or is older than the commit being merged. Reporting is the deliverable; blocking is explicitly not.

The check is OFFLINE-SAFE and never on the merge critical path. An unreachable network, an absent `gh`, or a repo with no remote produces an UNKNOWN verdict that is stated as unknown — never a pass. `check-engine-pin.sh`'s loud-SKIP discipline is the precedent: a run that could not measure must not read as a pass.

A repo that legitimately has no CI (no workflows at all) is NOT flagged. The finding is a declared-but-dead gate, not the absence of one — those are different situations and conflating them would make the check noise.
A test drives fixtures for each case: no workflows, workflows with a recent green run, workflows whose runs all failed to start, and workflows with no runs ever.
userStories.notes: test/cigate.sh PASS — 5 fixtures (no workflows at all / a recent green run / runs that completed with zero steps / a workflow with no runs ever / no GitHub remote), plus gh-absent, an API refusal, and a green run on another commit; every could-not-measure arm lands on UNKNOWN. bash -n clean across bin/chief + engine/*.sh + test/*.sh; smoke PASS, ratelimit PASS, noworkguard PASS, version-bump PASS (VERSION 0.9.3), doc-sync PASS (38 merged tasklists); quality ratchet OK (function_length_max 192 -> 200, tol 15). shellcheck not installed locally — CI enforces it. Counterfactual against the real portfolio: cuneiform 11/11 workflows DID NOT RUN, vita 1/1 DID NOT RUN, chief 1/1 DID NOT RUN, praxis RAN AND PASSED, pinakes 3 passed / 2 failed / 1 never run.

userStories.title: The trigger mismatch is detectable, because it is invisible otherwise
acceptanceCriteria: chief detects the vita shape: a workflow whose triggers cannot be produced by how chief lands work. chief merges locally and pushes the base branch, so a `pull_request`-only workflow is dead by construction under it, and nothing about the file looks wrong.

The report names the mismatch in the operator's terms — which trigger the workflow waits for, and what chief actually does — rather than printing YAML. 'Your CI waits for a pull request; chief pushes to main' is actionable, 'on: pull_request' is not.
Detection is textual and offline. Do not add a YAML dependency or a network call to the engine for this.
Counterfactual: pointing the check at vita's workflow as it stood on 2026-08-25 reports the mismatch. That file is the fixture.
userStories.notes: test/cigate.sh PASS — the counterfactual runs against test/fixtures/vita-ci-2026-08-25.yml, vita/.github/workflows/ci.yml copied byte for byte (sha256 317fb0bb…), and reports the mismatch naming both halves: what it waits for (a pull request, a manual dispatch) and what chief does (merges into main locally and pushes main). 11 more trigger fixtures cover every `on:` form (scalar / flow seq / block map / quoted "on" / block seq), a comment that only looks like a trigger, a branches filter, branches-ignore, tags-only, a declared CHIEF_BASE_BRANCH, and a file with no `on:` at all (unreadable, never a pass); plus a green run that does NOT clear a mismatch. Zero new tool dependencies and no network — the nogh-PATH arm of the existing suite caught the two I had added (tr, grep) and both are gone. Gates: bash -n clean across bin/chief + engine/*.sh + test/*.sh + install.sh; cigate PASS, smoke PASS, ratelimit PASS, noworkguard PASS, version-bump PASS (VERSION 0.9.4), doc-sync PASS (38 merged tasklists); doc-links 0 dead references; quality ratchet OK (function_length_max 192 -> 204, tol 15). shellcheck not installed locally — CI enforces it. Counterfactual against the real portfolio: vita 1/1 trigger mismatch (pull_request + workflow_dispatch), and 8 more the billing story would have hidden — cuneiform 3 (2 cron-only, 1 tags-only release), talos 3, pinakes 2 (1 cron-only, 1 workflow_dispatch-only); praxis 0.

userStories.title: The distinction is stated once, and reused
acceptanceCriteria: The three states are named and used consistently wherever chief reports a gate: RAN AND PASSED, RAN AND FAILED, DID NOT RUN. `.chief/verify.sh` already draws the skipped-vs-passed line locally; this extends the same idea outward rather than inventing a second vocabulary.

`docs/reference/verify-hook.md` records the rule and the measurement behind it, including that GitHub Actions is free for public repos and billed for private ones — the asymmetry that let this hide, since the public repos kept working and looked normal.

A merge record can be read afterwards to see which gates actually executed. A tasklist that merged while its declared CI never ran should be answerable from the record, because three of them already exist across this portfolio and were only found by hand.
userStories.notes: test/cigate.sh PASS — the merge record, both halves. STAMPED at merge (engine/lib.sh -> cigate_stamp_merge_record, offline and AFTER the merge commit exists): the local gate (hook ran / tasklist verify commands ran / NO_VERIFY=1 / no gate at all — the amphora shape — the last two recorded DID NOT RUN, never a pass) and the offline TRIGGER verdict per declared workflow, with whether CI then ran recorded UNKNOWN because no network call may sit on the merge path. READ BACK by `chief cigate --records`, which RECONSTRUCTS records written before the field from `git show <mergedToMain>:.github/workflows/…`. One vocabulary throughout — records carry the CIGATE_* tokens and cigate_label names them, asserted in the test. test/smoke.sh now asserts the stamp through the REAL merge path (it is in all three lists already). Gates: bash -n clean across bin/chief + engine/*.sh + test/*.sh + install.sh; cigate PASS, smoke PASS, ratelimit PASS, noworkguard PASS, version-bump PASS (VERSION 0.9.5), doc-sync PASS (38 merged tasklists), doc-links 0 dead references; quality ratchet OK (function_length_max 192 -> 206, tol 15; single_use_functions 21 -> 22, tol 2). shellcheck not installed locally — CI enforces it. Neutering cigate_stamp_merge_record makes the new block fail 7 assertions, so it does not pass by restating old behaviour. Counterfactual against the real portfolio (offline, no gh): vita 33 merged tasklists, 27 merged with a gate that DID NOT RUN — including 72-windows-linux-bundles, the one merged as auto-verified, now named off the file; cuneiform 354 of 378; talos 41 of 54; pinakes 36 of 41; praxis 0 of 23. Perf: cuneiform 70s -> 26s (all-trees memo instead of one-entry: 189 hits/189 misses -> 31 reads; printf -v instead of a fork per row; hoisted the per-iteration IFS substitution).
